text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky wants Austria's financial groups to be depoliticised.
- Austria's government plans to concentrate activities of the export industry in growth markets.
- Social Democrat Chancellor Vranitzky welcomes the return of conservative People's Party into the coalition after the sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria had threatened the government.
- The new banking giant made up of Bank Austria and Creditanstalt has a market power of over 50 percent. Austria's industry is sceptical of this overpowering group.
- Raiffeisen bank shows interest in Creditanstalt's stakes in regional banks and the government's stake in P.S.K.
DIE PRESSE
- The Vienna city government plans not to sell its Bank Austria shares but will reduce its stake through capital increases.
- Brussels demands more information on the sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria. A complaint lodged by the consortium around EA-Generali before Christmas is being checked.
- The Aktienforum group which represents investors has demanded more cash be offered to small share-holders of Creditanstalt after the takeover by Bank Austria.

- Nothing has changed in Moody's position on Bank Austria and City of Vienna ratings. In December the rating agency said it may downgrade them due to Bank Austria's takeover of Creditanstalt. Creditanstalt's ratings might however be improved.
- The end of the race for Creditanstalt made trading jump at Vienna's stock exchange on Monday.
- Siemens Austria received an order for six Chinese locomotives and the components for a further 34.
KURIER
- President Thomas Klestil supported the agreement between the coalition on the sale of Creditanstalt by saying he would dissolve Parliament should the coalition break.
- After failing to win the race for Creditanstalt, Die Erste savings bank plans to buy Bank Austria's stake in GiroCredit.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Creditanstalt's regional banks would prefer a German partner if sold.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Retailer Billa plans to open 54 new shops in 1997, investing 500 million schillings and creating 1000 jobs.
